note: The records that describe the DELIVERY layer rather than the cache. layout.json pins the directory and the naming convention; this pins the records, which were contractual and unpinned -- so a consumer modelled two record families, counted all three of these as unknown drift, and could not read a declared data loss. Every kind here must be a kind a consumer models.

cases.note: opens every segment; carries the identity the filename merely echoes
an attributable orphan: header survived, tail torn and discarded
an unattributable orphan: the crash took the header, so it belongs to no sequence and its span is coverage-indeterminate
declared loss -- segments 4 through 6 dropped under the disk cap. The magnitudes are illustrative; the shapes are the contract.
the same pass reclaiming a PREVIOUS run's segments: a second record, under that run's incarnation rather than the dropping process's. One record per incarnation is what keeps a range describable.

segment.note: one sealed segment as shipped. The header is first and every later record belongs to its incarnation; that containment is the contract, not a convention of this fixture. parquet_twin names the same records in the shipped Parquet form (spec 2.1), generated from this object by tools/gen-parquet-twin.py; decoding both to the same record sequence is what a reader proves.

orphan_segment.note: an unattributed orphan as shipped: segment_recovered first, then the records that survived. No segment_open, no incarnation, no continuity claim -- the span it covers is coverage-indeterminate by construction.
